items.article_search_text: Oscar Piastri knows that being willing to change things up can often lead to something better. He backed himself to make the switch to McLaren in 2022, and it paid off. That belief has driven his partnership with Google Pixel from day one, and in chapter three, independent creative agency Emotive shows what life looks Shot with production partner Somesuch, the work supports the launch of Google’s newest flagship smartphone – Pixel 11 Pro – and reunites director Isaac Lock with the team behind chapter one. The idea plays on a truth about Oscar. His schedule is packed. Every moment is accounted for. Every second is optimised. So Pixel 11 sweats the small stuff, leaving Oscar free to sweat the big stuff – like his intense training regime. The hero film is the first of a number of social-first assets, with the rest rolling out across Google Pixel and Oscar’s social channels. Each chapter has built on the last. Chapter one saw Oscar make the switch to Pixel, playing on his famously understated personality to show that refusing to settle leads to something better. Chapter two handed the work to his fans, turning a social vote into the ‘Pastry PiasTee’, a t-shirt Oscar wore at the Canadian Grand Prix and now sold as official merchandise. Chapter three shows the payoff, bringing Google Pixel’s global platform, ‘Ask more of your phone’, to life in the world’s most glamorous racing postcode. As with every chapter, the work was made for social first, designed to entertain like native content. Says Emma Dodd, Head of Devices & Services Marketing, Google AUNZ: “We’re excited to showcase how helpful and powerful our latest suite of Pixel 11 devices can be for Australians when they have access to Gemini Intelligence right in the palm of their hand. It was a pleasure to continue our partnership with Oscar to bring this chapter of work to life.” Says Rupert Taylor, Senior Creative Director, Emotive: “After the success of the first two chapters, we wanted to take a look at Oscar’s world post switch. We also wanted to stay true to his deadpan comedic stylings, and make some well crafted content that works well in the feed.” Says Isaac Lock, Director, Somesuch: “I always relish the challenge of creating a funny and engaging performance with someone who isn’t an actor, but Oscar makes it easy. He has a unique, deadpan tone and an unnerving unflappability that make him naturally funny when he’s just being himself.” Client: Google Pixel Creative Agency: Emotive Production: Somesuch Post Production: Emotive Productions & Arc Sound: Electric Sheep Music Register for FREE HERE and receive the Campaign Brief Daily Bulletin and/or the global Best Ads Best of the Week Bulletin. items.article_search_text: Sky Sports F1s Martin Brundle gives his verdict on Kimi Antonellis outstanding performance which puts him on the brink of becoming F1s youngest world champion and the struggles for McLarens Oscar Piastri and Mercedes George Russell Given that Red Bull and Ferrari, and from time to time McLaren, have undoubtedly closed down the pace advantage enjoyed by Mercedes in the first half of the season, it was looking possible that Kimi Antonelli might win the World Championship perhaps not fully in the style he would have wanted. His Austin qualifying and race performances demolished that concern in the most comprehensive way. From seemingly nowhere, he produced a stormer of an initial time in the third and final top-10 shootout to secure pole position and deny Max Verstappen's Red Bull and the two Ferraris of Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton, all of whom had seemed likely to beat him. It was his seventh pole of the season but his first since Spa back in the summer eight races ago, and therefore very timely. How Antonelli can win world title at Mexico City GP on Sunday Mexico City GP Schedule | F1 2026 standings | F1 2026 calendar Got the Sky Sports app? Sign up for latest F1 alerts Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream F1 with no contract 📺 Antonelli was 'simply outstanding' Kimi produced a perfect start and opening lap to comfortably lead, while the slow-starting Verstappen had to fend off the Ferraris. His pace, consistency, and tyre management thereafter was simply outstanding. Both Red Bull drivers, Verstappen and Isack Hadjar, had impressively made it through to Q3 having used only one set of soft tyres up to that point. This would give Max on the front row two brand new sets of soft tyres for the race, surely a significant advantage? As it turns out, not so, as they didn't last particularly well, forcing Max to pit first of everyone on Lap 13 of 56, and clearly now on a two-stop strategy. Mercedes didn't panic or respond, they trusted their data and instincts, and their championship-leading driver, to babysit his tyres at sufficient pace to make only one pit stop on Lap 24. With fresh tyres Max was inevitably very fast, and it initially appeared that he would be able to make up the extra 20 seconds he must spend in the pitlane for his second stop on Lap 31. But he couldn't clear the traffic with much ease. With his radio failing for the second time, but not before he would castigate his team for not moving his team-mate on a different run plan out of the way much sooner, he ended up a fairly disgruntled third. I did the post-race interviews and Max did though beam a nice smile when I complimented him on his overtake of Lando Norris up into Turn 1. It was pure Verstappen, just as he looked highly likely to lose a position to Leclerc, he converted that into an overtake of the McLaren with a stunning and controlled slice while extremely late on the brakes. It didn't do him much good in the end though because after Leclerc's own first stop on Lap 15, and having already been awesome on the opening lap of the race, he was mighty fast all the way to the chequered flag for a very well-earned second place. Ferrari had led all three practice sessions and so their qualifying had been a relative disappointment, but Hamilton too was rapid in the closing stages and would finish fourth just a second behind Verstappen. Another lap and he'd have joined his team-mate Leclerc on the podium. Norris did a fine job in fifth, having pitted on Lap 16 but then changing to a one-stopper, stretching his hard compound tyres a full 40 laps. In the end, he ran out of grip and slipped from second place, but it was good while it lasted. Piastri struggling with 2026 cars and Russell's 'harsh' penalty Oscar Piastri in the sister McLaren had another disappointing race, lacking front-running pace from relatively early on and finishing 52 seconds behind the winner. Oscar simply can't seem to gel with the 2026 cars and it's painful to witness after his stellar run last year. Piastri's struggles would heavily impact another driver having a season to forget in the shape of George Russell. On the opening lap Russell was both attacking Hadjar's slow-starting Red Bull and defending from Piastri. He ran wide at the Turn 12 hairpin at the end of the back straight and rejoined, marginally ahead of Piastri. The Stewards looked at all the camera angles and data and decided that Russell had gained a lasting advantage off the track by not losing a place to Piastri, but given it was the opening lap and the proximity of other cars, they served him half the normal 10-second penalty in mitigation. I thought that was harsh, George felt somewhat more strongly about it. Taking his five-second penalty at the first pit stop put him behind Piastri, and despite very solid initial pace on fresh tyres he simply couldn't find a way past the young Aussie and finished a full 54 seconds behind his winning team-mate in eighth place. Ouch. Another 11th for Audi! Liam Lawson drove very well again for two points at Racing Bulls in ninth and Pierre Gasly grabbed the final point for Alpine in 10th, the position he started. Nico Hulkenberg finished 11th and just out of the points - that's Audi's 10th race this year when just missing out. That's a torment which revives bad memories for me, back when points only went down to sixth place, I had a spate of dragging some reluctant machine past all the accidents and unreliability to finish a point-less seventh. Antonelli's supreme victory ensures he will be the youngest ever F1 world champion by over three years, usurping Sebastian Vettel. And the first Italian F1 world champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953, despite such motorsport passion and history in that country. Verstappen is now out of championship contention, incredibly for the first time since 2020. Russell and Hamilton would have to win every race until the end of the year, with Antonelli not showing up, for them to be champion. It's a case of when, and not if. Austin put on at great show at COTA, a combined 460,000 fans had all the usual great views along with live music, fun fairs, and many other attractions, and a spectacular hospitality suite and infinity pool at the very top of the already high first corner. The lucky few were transported over the track in gondolas on ski-slope-style pylons and cables, I'm impressed by how F1 keeps developing as a full experience, even though the race didn't turn out to be a classic. Next up, Mexico. MB Formula 1 next heads south for the second leg of The Americas triple header with the Mexico City Grand Prix this weekend, live on Sky Sports F1.
